newsitem.title: USA: Harris sees disappointing Q4 switch results.
newsitem.headline: Harris sees disappointing Q4 switch results.

text.p: Harris Corp said Wednesday that delays in high-margin foreign orders, combined with new product spending, will likely produce disappointing switch results through the fourth quarter ending June 30.

During the third quarter, the company said, the gain from the sale of investment securities was substantially offset by setbacks in the digital switch business, which saw orders pushed back into fiscal 1998.
Overall, Harris said, its communications sector had a 26 percent increase in income on a 10 percent rise in sales during the third quarter.

Company profits were $55.6 million, or $1.40 per share, an increase of 26 percent from a year earlier. Sales increased to $921.4 million from $875.9 million, and orders increased 11 percent to exceed shipments.
"We expect ot have another year of double-digit earnings growth for fiscal 1997," Harris said.
